raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Planted on the granite slopes of the Sierra de Gredos at high elevation, El Reventón pairs old-vine Garnacha with Alicante Henri Bouschet (a teinturier) and spends 14 months in oak on some vintages. The result is a deeply colored, high-energy red that reads both Mediterranean warmth and mountain freshness in the glass.",
  "wine_summary": "El Reventón matters because it blends two very different genetic profiles—old-vine Garnacha from Cebreros' granitic soils and Alicante Henri Bouschet, which brings pigmented pulp (teinturier varieties have colored flesh, not just colored skin). Comando G works biodynamically and labels the wine vegan, which signals low-intervention farming and no animal fining; that farming intensity concentrates fruit and savory detail. In practice, the wine shows dense dark fruit and firm tannic backbone from the teinturier influence, while altitude and sparse granite soils keep the palate lifted and savory rather than jammy.",
  "terroir_expression": "Cebreros sits on the granitic massif of the Sierra de Gredos: shallow, free-draining granite soils over fractured bedrock, with vineyards planted at 700–1,100m elevation. The continental-Mediterranean climate—hot, dry summers tempered by cool nights and a wide diurnal range—preserves acidity in Garnacha while allowing Alicante Henri Bouschet to ripen fully. Granite gives a stony framing and tensile acidity; the high altitude and thin soils produce concentrated dark fruit, firm tannins and a mineral/peppery savory thread in the finish.",
  "vinification_summary": "Fermentation focuses on extracting color and structure to match the teinturier character of Alicante Henri Bouschet; multiple vintages are aged 14 months in oak (barrel type unspecified) to integrate tannins and stabilize the wine. Because Alicante Henri Bouschet carries pigment in its pulp, color intensity and mid-palate density come from variety genetics as well as maceration choices—pigmented pulp increases extractable anthocyanins and tannin load compared with typical red-fleshed grapes.",
  "food_pairing": "Nashville hot chicken — the wine's ripe dark fruit and alcohol cut through the spice while tannins handle the fried exterior. Roasted leg of lamb with rosemary and garlic — savory herbs echo the wine's granite-driven minerality and tannin binds with lamb fat. Cochinillo (suckling pig with crisp skin) — the tactile crunch and fatty meat balance the wine's structure and concentrated fruit. Aged Manchego and membrillo — salt and fat from the cheese tame tannins and let the wine's darker fruit show. Beef short rib confit with smoked paprika — the wine's intensity and oak-aged spice stand up to braised richness.",
  "comparable_wines": "Alto Moncayo 'Moncayo' — a high-impact, concentrated Garnacha from Campo de Borja that shares power, dark fruit density and oak presence though from a lower-altitude, more arid terroir; useful as a benchmark for concentration. Bodegas Borsao 'Tres Picos' — an accessible, fruit-forward Garnacha from Campo de Borja that contrasts El Reventón's mountain acidity but offers a reference for price-to-intensity among Spanish Garnachas.",
  "style_profile": "Alicante Henri Bouschet–Garnacha full-bodied dry red with firm tannins and intense color",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink from 2–12 years after vintage; store at 12–14°C with stable humidity and minimal vibration. Open decanting (30–60 minutes) benefits younger vintages to soften oak and tannin.",
  "value_assessment": "Price: $40–70 retail, depending on vintage and market. At that range, Alto Moncayo competes at the upper end while Borsao Tres Picos sits well below; El Reventón is worth the price if you prioritize high color, dense fruit and aging tannic structure from a Cebreros site—buy for cellar potential or for restaurants seeking concentrated Spanish reds.",
  "market_position": "Serious restaurant lists and independent wine shops that emphasize single-vineyard Sierra de Gredos bottlings stock El Reventón; collectors who chase high-scoring, site-driven Spanish reds also buy it for verticals. It sits between approachable supermarket Garnachas and premium single-vineyard offerings—appealing to drinkers who want intensity with a terroir signature.",
  "insider_take": "This is a wine for drinkers who want power with altitude-driven freshness; if you expect perfumed, low-alcohol Garnacha, skip it. Most buyers underplay the role of Alicante Henri Bouschet here—the variety is the engine of color and tannin, so expect inky visuals and a firmer grip than classic skin-pigmented Garnacha.",

parsed.hook: Planted on the granite slopes of the Sierra de Gredos at high elevation, El Reventón pairs old-vine Garnacha with Alicante Henri Bouschet (a teinturier) and spends 14 months in oak on some vintages. The result is a deeply colored, high-energy red that reads both Mediterranean warmth and mountain freshness in the glass.
parsed.wine_summary: El Reventón matters because it blends two very different genetic profiles—old-vine Garnacha from Cebreros' granitic soils and Alicante Henri Bouschet, which brings pigmented pulp (teinturier varieties have colored flesh, not just colored skin). Comando G works biodynamically and labels the wine vegan, which signals low-intervention farming and no animal fining; that farming intensity concentrates fruit and savory detail. In practice, the wine shows dense dark fruit and firm tannic backbone from the teinturier influence, while altitude and sparse granite soils keep the palate lifted and savory rather than jammy.
parsed.terroir_expression: Cebreros sits on the granitic massif of the Sierra de Gredos: shallow, free-draining granite soils over fractured bedrock, with vineyards planted at 700–1,100m elevation. The continental-Mediterranean climate—hot, dry summers tempered by cool nights and a wide diurnal range—preserves acidity in Garnacha while allowing Alicante Henri Bouschet to ripen fully. Granite gives a stony framing and tensile acidity; the high altitude and thin soils produce concentrated dark fruit, firm tannins and a mineral/peppery savory thread in the finish.
parsed.vinification_summary: Fermentation focuses on extracting color and structure to match the teinturier character of Alicante Henri Bouschet; multiple vintages are aged 14 months in oak (barrel type unspecified) to integrate tannins and stabilize the wine. Because Alicante Henri Bouschet carries pigment in its pulp, color intensity and mid-palate density come from variety genetics as well as maceration choices—pigmented pulp increases extractable anthocyanins and tannin load compared with typical red-fleshed grapes.
parsed.food_pairing: Nashville hot chicken — the wine's ripe dark fruit and alcohol cut through the spice while tannins handle the fried exterior. Roasted leg of lamb with rosemary and garlic — savory herbs echo the wine's granite-driven minerality and tannin binds with lamb fat. Cochinillo (suckling pig with crisp skin) — the tactile crunch and fatty meat balance the wine's structure and concentrated fruit. Aged Manchego and membrillo — salt and fat from the cheese tame tannins and let the wine's darker fruit show. Beef short rib confit with smoked paprika — the wine's intensity and oak-aged spice stand up to braised richness.
parsed.comparable_wines: Alto Moncayo 'Moncayo' — a high-impact, concentrated Garnacha from Campo de Borja that shares power, dark fruit density and oak presence though from a lower-altitude, more arid terroir; useful as a benchmark for concentration. Bodegas Borsao 'Tres Picos' — an accessible, fruit-forward Garnacha from Campo de Borja that contrasts El Reventón's mountain acidity but offers a reference for price-to-intensity among Spanish Garnachas.
parsed.style_profile: Alicante Henri Bouschet–Garnacha full-bodied dry red with firm tannins and intense color
parsed.cellar_recommendation: Drink from 2–12 years after vintage; store at 12–14°C with stable humidity and minimal vibration. Open decanting (30–60 minutes) benefits younger vintages to soften oak and tannin.
parsed.value_assessment: Price: $40–70 retail, depending on vintage and market. At that range, Alto Moncayo competes at the upper end while Borsao Tres Picos sits well below; El Reventón is worth the price if you prioritize high color, dense fruit and aging tannic structure from a Cebreros site—buy for cellar potential or for restaurants seeking concentrated Spanish reds.
parsed.market_position: Serious restaurant lists and independent wine shops that emphasize single-vineyard Sierra de Gredos bottlings stock El Reventón; collectors who chase high-scoring, site-driven Spanish reds also buy it for verticals. It sits between approachable supermarket Garnachas and premium single-vineyard offerings—appealing to drinkers who want intensity with a terroir signature.
parsed.insider_take: This is a wine for drinkers who want power with altitude-driven freshness; if you expect perfumed, low-alcohol Garnacha, skip it. Most buyers underplay the role of Alicante Henri Bouschet here—the variety is the engine of color and tannin, so expect inky visuals and a firmer grip than classic skin-pigmented Garnacha.
